cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Artificial ≠ natural – made by humans rather than occurring naturally.

p.em: Example: AI programs can write simple texts very fast.

cosy-blockquote.p: Brain ≠ computer – the organ in the head that controls thought and memory.

p.em: Example: Your brain needs practice to stay smart.

cosy-blockquote.p: Turn off ≠ turn on – to stop a machine or device from working.

p.em: Example: I turn off my computer before going to sleep.

cosy-blockquote.p: Depend ≠ standalone – to need someone or something for help.

p.em: Example: Many students depend on spell checkers.

cosy-blockquote.p: Memory ≠ forgetting – the ability to remember things.

p.em: Example: Writing by hand improves your memory.

cosy-blockquote.p: Calculate ≠ guess – to discover an amount using numbers.

p.em: Example: He can calculate simple math problems mentally.

cosy-blockquote.p: Screen ≠ paper – the flat display surface on a device.

p.em: Example: Staring at a phone screen all day tires your eyes.

cosy-blockquote.p: Practice ≠ laziness – doing an activity repeatedly to improve.

p.em: Example: Daily math practice keeps your mind sharp.

cosy-blockquote.p: Skill ≠ ignorance – the ability to do something well.

p.em: Example: Navigating without GPS is a useful map skill.

cosy-blockquote.p: Smart ≠ foolish – having or showing quick intelligence.

p.em: Example: Solving puzzles keeps seniors smart and active.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Do you think people depend too much on smartphone apps today?
★ What app do you use most frequently every day?

Can you calculate simple shopping prices without using a phone calculator?
★ How good are you at mental math?

How does turning off screens for a day help your brain rest?
★ Have you ever tried spending a Sunday without internet?

What digital skill would you miss most if technology stopped working?
★ Can you find locations using a printed map?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Schools should ban AI tools for homework writing. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Did you write your homework by hand when you were young?

People would become smarter if we turned off AI for a week. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What would be hardest about living without AI for one week?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation with teacher in 1-on-1 format.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ol.li:
Schools should ban AI tools for homework writing. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Did you write your homework by hand when you were young?

People would become smarter if we turned off AI for a week. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What would be hardest about living without AI for one week?

ul.li: Incorrect: We should to turn off AI. → Correct: We should turn off AI. ((Modal verb 'should' is followed by base verb without 'to'.))
Incorrect: My brain is need rest. → Correct: My brain needs rest. ((Use standard present simple verb 'needs'.))

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Reflection & Feedback: Review language highlights and key corrections with your teacher.
